CHAPTER V
OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES OF REGIONAL GOVERNMENT Article 17 (1) The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to implement efforts to prevent the occurrence of violence against women and children, in the form of:
a. collecting data and organizing an information system for the protection of women and children victims of violence;

c. disseminating laws and regulations related to the empowerment of women and protection of child victims of violence.
(2) The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to provide and organize services for Victims in the form of: a. establishing and organizing technical service institutions for Victims by involving community elements; and
b. encouraging community awareness of the importance of protection for Victims of violence.

Paragraph 1
Prevention of Violence against Children

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Protection of women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by giving consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
2. Protection of children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, as well as receive protection from violence and discrimination.
3. Women is a person who is female in gender. 4. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
5. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence occurring in the Regional territory.
6. Violence is any act against women and children that results in the emergence of misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully.
7. Empowerment of women is the strengthening of women victims of violence to be able to strive and work independently after being recovered and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.
8. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society.
9. Social rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological and social conditions in order to be able to carry out their role again properly both in the family and in society.
10. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with their families and communities.
11. Assistance is an activity to provide counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims carried out by a person or representative from an institution that has expertise.
12. Prevention is the effort of the government together with families and communities as well as the private sector and/or business world to prevent the occurrence of violence through socialization, education, advocacy and promotion activities.
13. Handling is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing, and knowing that violence against victims will, is, and/or has occurred.
14. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy, and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
15. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree.
16. Integrated Service Center for the Protection of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is a technical implementing unit of the Regional Apparatus that carries out technical operational activities and/or technical supporting activities for integrated services for women and children victims of violence.
17. Forum for the Protection of Victims of Violence, hereinafter abbreviated as FPKK, is a coordination forum for prevention, handling and empowerment of victims of violence against women and children whose implementation is carried out in a networked manner and is formed at the Regional, sub-district, and village levels.
18. Region is Sleman Regency.
19. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
20. Regent is the Regent of Sleman.
21. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and DPRD in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Region.

Paragraph 3
Empowerment of Women Victims of Violence

Article 12
(1) Prevention of violence against children as referred to in Article 11 letter a is implemented among others by:
a. forming a network in efforts to prevent violence against children;
b. conducting coordination, integration, synchronization of violence prevention based on partnership patterns with the community, private sector and Non-Governmental Organizations; and
c. disseminating laws and regulations related to the protection of child victims of violence.
(2) Prevention of violence against children as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out in an integrated manner and coordinated by Regional Apparatus that has the main duties and functions in the field of women's empowerment and child protection.

Article 4
(1) The objectives of protection for women victims of violence are directed to: a. create conditions that support the development of the potential of women victims of violence;
b. strengthen the potential already possessed by women victims of violence; and
c. improve the work skills of women victims of violence.
(2) The objectives of protection for child victims of violence are directed to: a. provide social rehabilitation for child victims of violence; b. reunite child victims of violence with their family and/or environment; and
c. improve the empowerment of child victims of violence.

ELUCIDATION
OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF SLEMAN REGENCY
NUMBER 2 OF 2017
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL
Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Economic factors, social environment and technological development have a major influence on the increase of such acts of violence. This condition demands the Regional Government to take concrete steps through program activities as efforts to prevent and protect women and children from acts of violence.

One of the efforts to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women while maintaining their role and nature as women to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.

Efforts to prevent the occurrence of violence against children are the obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector. Community services are the front line when there is potential violence against children. The mechanism for violence prevention efforts and protection of child victims of violence involves multi-sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. The intended efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and children victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the Regional area, it is necessary to regulate this in a Regional Regulation.

4.4.rationale: The original Indonesian regulation clearly includes education as a prevention measure. Pasal 1 angka 12 defines “Pencegahan” as efforts to prevent violence through “sosialisasi, edukasi, advokasi dan promosi.” Additionally, Pasal 17 ayat (1) huruf b obligates the Regional Government to prevent violence by “melakukan pendidikan tentang nilai anti kekerasan terhadap perempuan dan anak” (conduct education on anti-violence values). The retrieved candidates contained these provisions, and the judge’s Yes rationale matches the source text. Therefore the golden label “No” appears incorrect.

5.6.translated_snippet: Letter c What is meant by "socialization" is the dissemination of information on laws and regulations carried out through mass media, electronic media, and/or direct counseling to the community.
5.6.evaluator_rationale: The policy explicitly references dissemination of information through mass media and electronic media as part of socialization activities, indicating recognition/engagement of media in prevention-related communication.

# BUPATI SLEMAN REGULATION
NUMBER 78 OF 2016

REGARDING

# AMENDMENT TO BUPATI SLEMAN REGULATION NUMBER 68 OF 2014 REGARDING PROCEDURES FOR GRANTING INCENTIVES AND DISINCENTIVES IN THE IMPLEMENTATION OF SPATIAL PLANNING

WITH THE BLESSING OF ALMIGHTY GOD

BUPATI SLEMAN,

Considering : a. that to implement the provisions of Article 38 paragraph (4) of Bupati Sleman Regulation Number 68 of 2014 regarding Procedures for Granting Incentives and Disincentives in the Implementation of Spatial Planning, it is necessary to make amendments;

b. that based on the considerations as referred to in letter a, it is necessary to establish a Bupati Sleman Regulation regarding Amendment to Bupati Sleman Regulation Number 68 of 2014 regarding Procedures for Granting Incentives and Disincentives in the Implementation of Spatial Planning;

In view of : 1. Law Number 15 of 1950 regarding the Establishment of Yogyakarta Special Region (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 1950 Number 3, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 10) as amended by Law Number 9 of 1955 regarding Amendment to Law Number 15 of 1950 (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 1955 Number 43, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 827);

2. Law Number 26 of 2007 regarding Spatial Planning (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2007 Number 68, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 4725);

3. Law Number 13 of 2012 regarding Yogyakarta Special Region Privileges (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2012 Number 170, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 5339);

4. Law Number 23 of 2014 regarding Regional Government (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2014 Number 244, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 5587) as amended several times, most recently by Law Number 9 of 2015 regarding Second Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2014 regarding Regional Government (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2015 Number 58, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 5679);

5. Government Regulation Number 32 of 1950 regarding the Establishment of Regencies within the Yogyakarta Special Region Environment;

6. Government Regulation Number 15 of 2010 regarding Implementation of Spatial Planning (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2010 Number 21, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 5103);

7. Bupati Sleman Regulation Number 68 of 2014 regarding Procedures for Granting Incentives and Disincentives in the Implementation of Spatial Planning (Sleman Regency Gazette of 2014 Number 68);

HAS DECIDED:

To establish : BUPATI REGULATION REGARDING AMENDMENT TO BUPATI SLEMAN REGULATION NUMBER 68 OF 2014 REGARDING PROCEDURES FOR GRANTING INCENTIVES AND DISINCENTIVES IN THE IMPLEMENTATION OF SPATIAL PLANNING.

Article I

Several provisions in Bupati Sleman Regulation Number 68 of 2014 regarding Procedures for Granting Incentives and Disincentives in the Implementation of Spatial Planning (Sleman Regency Gazette of 2014 Number 68) are amended as follows:

1. The provisions of Article 1 are amended, so that Article 1 reads as follows:

Article 1

In this Bupati Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Regency is Sleman Regency.
2. Regency Government is Sleman Regency Government.
3. Bupati is the Bupati of Sleman.
4. Regional Apparatus Organization, hereinafter abbreviated as OPD, is an element supporting the Bupati and the Regional People's Representative Council in administering Regional Government Affairs which are the authority of the Region.
5. Spatial Planning is a system of spatial planning processes, spatial utilization, and spatial utilization control.
6. Spatial Planning is a form of spatial structure and spatial pattern.
7. Spatial Structure is the arrangement of settlement centers and network systems of infrastructure and facilities that function as supporters of socio-economic activities of the community which hierarchically have functional relationships.
8. Spatial Pattern is the distribution of space allocation in an area which includes space allocation for protection functions and space allocation for cultivation functions.
9. Spatial Utilization is efforts to realize the spatial structure and spatial pattern in accordance with the Spatial Planning through the preparation and implementation of programs along with their financing.
10. Spatial Utilization Control is efforts to realize the implementation of Spatial Planning in accordance with the Spatial Planning that has been established.
11. Incentive is a reward for activities that are in accordance with the Spatial Planning.
12. Disincentive is a penalty for activities that are not in accordance with the Spatial Planning.
13. Compensation is compensation for the limitation of spatial utilization that must be given to affected parties.
14. Spatial Planning Permit is a permit granted to a person or entity to deviate from the provisions of the Spatial Planning.
15. Spatial Planning Sanction is an administrative action imposed on violators of the Spatial Planning.

2. The provisions of Article 38 are amended, so that Article 38 reads as follows:

Article 38

(1) Disincentives as referred to in Article 3 letter b are given in the form of:
a. limitation on the provision of infrastructure and facilities;
b. imposition of compensation;
c. application of disincentive fiscal instruments; and/or
d. cancellation of incentives.

(2) Limitation on the provision of infrastructure and facilities as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a is carried out by:
a. not providing new infrastructure and facilities; and/or
b. limiting the quality and/or quantity of infrastructure and facilities services.

(3) Imposition of compensation as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b is carried out by imposing compensation on parties who utilize space that causes changes in spatial use that are not in accordance with the Spatial Planning.

(4) Application of disincentive fiscal instruments as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c is carried out in the form of:
a. imposition of local taxes at the highest rate in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations; and/or
b. imposition of local levies at the highest rate in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

(5) Cancellation of incentives as referred to in paragraph (1) letter d is carried out by canceling the incentives that have been given to parties who violate the provisions of the Spatial Planning.

Article II

This Bupati Regulation comes into force on the date of promulgation.

In order that everyone may know of it, the promulgation of this Bupati Regulation is ordered by its placement in the Sleman Regency Gazette.

7.1.rationale: The original Indonesian text does not establish a dedicated local-government budget/funding source (e.g., APBD) for implementation. The cited evidence comes from the elucidation of Pasal 24 ayat (2) (about village-level forums) stating that facilitation by the Village Government includes “memberikan pembiayaan” (providing financing) for activities/monitoring/evaluation. This indicates possible village facilitation costs, but it is not a clear statement of a formal local government budget allocation/source for the policy’s programs (and it is about village government facilitation, not necessarily regency budget). Given the indicator is “Local government budget,” the judge overgeneralized from a narrow ‘financing’ mention to conclude a budget/funding source exists. So the information in candidates does not robustly support Yes, and the false positive is best explained by evaluation failure (overly lenient inference).
